priorities.finding: Prioritize request-context fields tab, hour, and weekday. Training-only screening showed a positive primary lift of 0.00221 with full coverage; daily lift was positive on 3 of 4 holdout dates, although variability was larger than the mean. The completed experiment achieved GAUC 0.6670 and primary 0.6014, supporting a modest but plausible within-user ranking benefit.
priorities.recommended_action: Keep request context as the only feature-group addition for the next confirmation run. Do not spend additional budget on the screened reject groups before confirming this gain on a fresh temporal split.

priorities.finding: Investigate tab-specific weakness, especially tabs 8 and 3. Their GAUC values are 0.278 and 0.500, respectively, with very low nDCG@5 and large negative primary deltas versus global performance. This is a top-five and within-user ranking problem rather than merely a classification issue.
priorities.recommended_action: Use tab-aware diagnostics or a targeted follow-up for these slices only after confirmation of the global request-context effect; avoid broad feature expansion.

priorities.finding: Cold or sparse-positive users are a material diagnostic weakness. The zero-positive slice has GAUC 0.5 and zero top-five metrics, while one- through four-positive users have much stronger top-five metrics despite only moderate GAUC. Interpret this primarily as sparse-label and candidate-ranking difficulty, not evidence that request context is harmful.
priorities.recommended_action: Monitor sparse-positive cohorts separately and report GAUC alongside nDCG@5, MAP@5, and Recall@5; do not optimize against the zero-positive slice using retrospective labels.

avoid: Reject user_profile, historical_user_author_affinity, upload_recency, content_duration, item_metadata, historical_author_response, and historical_item_response for this budget cycle based on training-only screening: screen:user_profile, screen:historical_user_author_affinity, screen:upload_recency, screen:content_duration, screen:item_metadata, screen:historical_author_response, screen:historical_item_response.

Avoid interpreting high top-five metrics in tiny segments as robust evidence when GAUC is weak or the sample is very small, as illustrated by experiment:1:segment:tab:10 and experiment:1:segment:user_active_degree:UNKNOWN.
Avoid all current-impression outcome fields and aggregate snapshots lacking per-impression availability timestamps; they are leakage risks and are not eligible for ranking.
metric_diagnosis: The request-context result is directionally positive but small relative to daily variability, so it merits confirmation rather than immediate broad rollout. Overall GAUC of 0.6670 indicates useful within-user ordering, while the weakest tab slices show that top-five quality can fail even when global metrics are acceptable. Treat GAUC as the primary stability signal, use nDCG@5 and related top-five metrics to localize user-facing failures, and stop further feature-group exploration until the request-context effect is confirmed on a new temporal holdout.
